svg.aria-label: How the scheduled retrospective borrows an enrolled user's token, and how the async ingestion pipeline carries identity as data without a token
svg.title: Identity when no one is clicking
svg.text: Identity when no one is clicking
Two parts of Strobe run without a person at the keyboard. The scheduled run borrows a real user's token so it can use the normal path;
the ingestion pipeline needs no token at all, because identity was checked at upload time and now travels as data.
A Scheduled retrospective — borrow a real user's identity
lambda-retro.py
EventBridge Scheduler fires
Retro Lambda reads the enrolled logins

text.tspan: → { accounts: [ { email, password } ] } — the only real credential

svg.text: Logs in exactly like the browser does
V2
Opens the SAME agent WebSocket
V3
Agent calls MCP with that user's token

text.tspan: same tools, same TokenClaim("sub") filter — it can only
read the enrolled user's own posts

svg.text: V1
Saves the result as that user

text.tspan: Bearer token → a 24 h Moment in their app

svg.text: Why passwords in a secret? (the honest limitation)
Cognito won't issue a user's token to a service without that user's credentials.
Client-credentials (machine-to-machine) tokens exist, but they are access tokens whose
sub is the app client, not a person — useless for a per-user filter. A custom-auth
Lambda trigger flow could do it properly; out of scope, so only enrolled accounts run.
B Async ingestion — identity becomes data
upload Lambda (A1) → S3 → SQS → lambda-sqs-worker.py
V1
Browser asks for an upload URL — token checked here

text.tspan: upload Lambda builds the key from the verified claims:
— the client cannot choose the sub part

svg.text: Browser PUTs the bytes straight to S3

text.tspan: no token: the presigned URL's signature IS the permission,
for that one key, for 240 s

svg.text: S3 event → SQS → worker Lambda

text.tspan: runs under its own IAM role; Cognito is not involved at all

svg.text: Worker recovers the owner from the key
Owner is written next to the vector
Later, MCP filters on exactly that field

text.tspan: with sub from a verified token (V3)

svg.text: Why this is still safe without a token
The token is checked once, at the edge (V1). From then on the owner travels as data
that only AWS-authorised code can write: the S3 key and the SQS message. Text jobs
work the same way — the post Lambda puts the verified userId in the SQS message.
Trust the data because of WHO could write it, not because of a token in hand.
TWO KINDS OF IDENTITY RUN THROUGH THE WHOLE SYSTEM

The agent holds no secrets: it never has AWS keys (task role), never a model API key (Bedrock is IAM-authorised), and only ever borrows the user's token for one connection.
